Fixed legal parameter/sign slots span every N×N target by varying only phase weights. The explicit (++,-+,+-,--)=(N−2,1,1,N−2) architecture uses same-sign nodes q²,…,q^(N−1), cross-sign nodes 1, beta=1 and guards −1, entirely in k. This optimizes universal target-independent slots, not target-adaptive Fourier minima; the N11 upper bound 14 remains stronger than the universal specialization 20. Separately over C, the full legal finite-node bank rank of S^−1 is N−1 but its ordinary/Zariski border rank is 1; exact attainment uses Q(q,zeta_(N−1)). This is an inverse-shift boundary example, not a Fourier rank gap. Bank counts are not scans or arithmetic work. The omitted-infinite-endpoint mechanism is classical in spirit; exact specialized priority remains unconfirmed, with no FFT runtime claim.
changes.append: [2026-10-10 16:11 UTC; accepted scoped refinements] Base-field Fourier bound accepted: for every odd N≥7 and K=Q(q), q primitive of order N, M_K(F_N)≤2N−4 using (N−3,1,1,N−3) orientations and fully split distinct nonzero K-nodes. tw G([[A,E],[P,0]]) >= ceil(N/4)-1 for totally nonsingular N by N targets. Fixed h-vertex-minor-free extensions require Q>=ceil(N/4)^2/h^3. Every target has a planar maximum-degree-four realization with M=3N^2+2N.

[2026-10-10 13:00 UTC; reviewed scoped continuation] v30 related-family continuation under the preserved SCHUR-V28 identity; these are distinct direct-coordinate statements, not a restatement or recount of v28 treewidth or v29 denominator support. Accepted source core: dense off-diagonal targets force two exact triangular-sum orders to reverse; for a totally nonsingular target the necessary correction-rank/LIS gate is rank(R)>=floor(LIS/2). Same-branch interface dimension q>=floor(N/2) requires total nonsingularity in the actual field; complex prime Fourier is a valid case. Invertible cross-branch N-by-N targets require q>=N. Actual baseline coordinates must retain the proved triangular zero pattern; arbitrary endpoint maps need not preserve it. The LIS gate is necessary, not a sufficient or uniformly sharp characterization. Independent refinements accepted: every totally nonsingular target admits minimum-rank floor(N/2) strict-upper completion with invertible triangular residual; shared zero rectangles can be stronger than LIS; reordered complex F4 has a rank-one correction/invertible triangular baseline, disproving a blanket composite-Fourier floor(N/2) assertion; one-sided Jacobi rectangle bounds allow a singular branch pivot when the whole bordered system is invertible, without using the nonexistent branch inverse. Corrected finite-field examples (N,p)=(9,19),(11,23),(13,53) are not totally nonsingular; their individual realizations remain valid, with exhaustive full-spark evidence confined to (5,11),(7,29). No improved solve cost, unrestricted Fourier bound, numerical guarantee or novelty claim. Source archive SHA-256: ce2fba707468da831596f7bd74653ac59221a43707559ccf80724d89f4bde916. [2026-10-10 14:03 UTC; accepted reviews] Related v31 support review accepted: the totally nonsingular forced half-rectangle requires superconcentrator support in the complete normalized scalar DAG. Edge-depth 2/3 bounds are Omega(N log^2 N/log log N) / Omega(N log log N), with unbounded fan-in. Generic infinite-field weights do not supply Fourier weights; arbitrary finite fields and unsorted-edge depth code need the stated guards.

Accepted Schur–q-defect gate: fixed linear pieces sharing nullity-one D obey rank(sum C_j)<=1+sum k_j under uniform defect bounds. One common input has total defects >=max(0,r-1). Omega(nr) work follows only with independent additive charges >=c*n*(1+actual defects). Shared computation, adaptive/nonlinear factors, tabulation and FFT fallback are excluded. No unrestricted FFT lower bound or novelty claim. Sources: accepted 13:40 support review and independent 13:52 q-defect review.

[2026-10-10 14:35 UTC; related v32 source audit] For prime p in the pure pth-root-weight scalar DAG model, each exact Fourier entry has 1 mod p paths; nonunique realizations need at least p+1. At most p paths per pair therefore forces uniqueness and at least p² edges, with distinct disjoint terminals. Positive rational amplitudes retain target-phase/alphabet coverage, not the integer count gap. Arbitrary positive real amplitudes break that extension: depth-one F5 has 33 edges, palette {1,ζ²,ζ³}, and amplitudes 1 or φ=(1+sqrt(5))/2 for ζ=exp(±2πi/5). The proposed exact Gauss–superconcentrator O(N log log N) construction remains open: an actual uniform sparse graph and exact weighted-fiber identity with t-independent, separable or explicitly charged pair amplitudes are still missing. General scalar weights and Gauss normalization are outside the pure-root gate. No exact FFT upper bound, historical-priority claim or identification with the v28 theorem; the accepted approximate packed theorem is unchanged.

[2026-10-10; reviewed 14:53 cycle] Related v32 amplitude-field refinement: for odd prime p, real K, L=K∩Q(ζp) and h=[Q(ζp):L], mandatory phase coverage holds iff L=Q. The sharp global positive-K depth-one palette is h+1; conditioned on that minimum palette, sharp edge count is (2p−1)+h(p−1)(p−h). For fixed number-field K, only primes dividing disc(K) can escape coverage. Separately, strict X→U→V→Y Gauss graphs with a latent label on every middle edge, nonzero fibers for every (i,j,t), and the pointwise character-rectangle law with fixed endpoint gauges (or an explicitly certified every-path exponent law) need at least 2p²+p edges, attained by the dense construction. This does not cover general aggregate weighted fibers, composite lengths or broader graphs. The sparse aggregate Gauss construction and historical novelty remain open; no general FFT lower bound or speedup.

[2026-10-10 15:35 UTC; accepted supplements] Related prime-complex aggregate-basis supplement: for square invertible boundary matrices A,C and separately counted latent middle-edge colors, put r_t=nnz((C^−1F)[:,t]), s_t=nnz((FA^−1)[t,:]) and delta_X=nnz(X^−1)−nnz(X). Beating 2p²+p edges requires delta_A+delta_C>sum_t(r_t−1)(s_t−1); this is necessary, not a sparse construction. Separately, the exact positive-rational phase gate is not approximation-robust: three global pth-root phases with positive rational amplitudes approximate F_p arbitrarily closely in relative operator norm, at quadratic edge cost. At most two global rays with nonnegative amplitudes have relative operator gap at least 1/3, for depth one or a proven common output cone, without free endpoint gauges. Roots remain exact supplied phases; no finite-word executor, fast transform or historical priority is established. Statement-level audit: the amplitude coverage and h+1 palette are classical-corollary synthesis (Galois, Chebotarev and positive-cone geometry); the period moments are known. Combined-formulation and sharp two-ray priority remain unresolved; no demonstrated breakthrough.
changes.append: [2026-10-10 16:11 UTC; accepted scoped refinements] Related square-invertible, separately colored aggregate Gauss model: an explicit disjoint-four-chain family has E=2p²+p−floor(p/4) for every prime p≥5. At p5, the single-chain ledger is 25 input + 8 output + 21 colored middle edges =54; global optimality is not proved. Its fibers aggregate correctly, but the strict pointwise character law fails even with fixed endpoint gauges, so the prior strict-model 2p²+p theorem is unchanged. An invertible one-sided endpoint basis with at most p+2 nonzeros cannot improve the dense count; the p+3 first-sparsity threshold is sharp. At p3 the full square-invertible aggregate minimum is 21. The family still uses dense A=F and quadratic construction/evaluation; no subquadratic FFT or historical novelty is established.
